title: Modi Told a Packed Melbourne Arena He'd Made a 'Hat-Trick.' Outside, Anti-Indian Protesters Were Waiting.
excerpt: The Prime Minister's third Australian visit drew thousands of cheering diaspora members — and a far-right fringe demanding Indians leave. AustralianSuper committed $347 million to India's infrastructure fund the same day.
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed thousands of Indians at a packed arena in Melbourne on Wednesday evening, calling it a "housefull blockbuster" and declaring his third Australian visit a "hat-trick" that proves the relationship between the two countries has reached "great heights."

## A Living Bridge, Under Strain

Outside the venue, a different scene unfolded. Around two dozen far-right protesters shouted anti-immigration slogans and held banners calling for the expulsion of Indians from Australia. They were heavily outnumbered by flag-waving supporters, but their presence underscored a growing tension in a country where roughly one million people claim Indian ancestry out of a population of 28 million.

Modi chose warmth over confrontation. "The weather in Melbourne may be cold but the warmth of the welcome from the Indian community was truly unforgettable," he wrote on X. "We Indians are just like sugar dissolving in milk, making it even sweeter."

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, who introduced Modi at the community event, called the Indian leader a "living bridge" between the two nations. "The energy that we feel here defines the Australia-India partnership," Albanese said. "It is enthusiasm, dynamism that drives positivity and promise of our two nations and peoples."

## Half a Billion Dollars Follows Modi to Melbourne

The visit was not purely ceremonial. Australia's largest pension fund, AustralianSuper, announced it would invest an additional A$500 million (approximately $347 million) in India's National Investment and Infrastructure Fund — a vote of institutional confidence at a time when global capital is jittery over the Iran crisis.

The uranium deal signed a day earlier had already made headlines, ending a twelve-year stalemate, but the AustralianSuper commitment signals something broader: Australian institutional money is flowing into India in serious volumes, and the relationship is being reframed as an economic partnership, not just a diplomatic one.

India is already Australia's fifth-largest trading partner after China, Japan, the United States, and South Korea. A Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement is currently under negotiation and is expected to deepen that integration.

## Why It Matters for the Diaspora

For the million-strong Indian community in Australia, Modi's visit carries weight beyond the photo opportunities. Anti-Indian sentiment — fuelled by debates over immigration levels, student visa fraud allegations, and social media clips that went viral — has become a persistent background anxiety for Indians living in cities like Melbourne, Sydney, and Brisbane.

The far-right protesters outside the Modi event were a small group, but their visibility matters. It echoes the anti-Indian sentiment Modi was warned about before arriving, particularly in New Zealand, where he heads Friday afternoon.

At the same time, diaspora community leaders expressed optimism. Anou Khanijou McPherson, president of the Australia India Society of Victoria, called the visit "the start of building a bridge between both of our countries" and highlighted complementary strengths in technology, education, and trade.

## A Twelve-Year Gap in Melbourne

Modi's last visit to Melbourne was twelve years ago. He addressed a packed Sydney stadium in 2023, but this was his first engagement with the Melbourne community since 2014 — the first time an Indian prime minister had visited Australia in 28 years.

"When I visited Australia in 2014, it was the first time an Indian Prime Minister had visited in 28 years," Modi told the crowd. "And you might recall I said then that you would not have to wait another 28 years. This is my third visit in the last twelve years."

Heavy police presence was visible around the venue throughout the evening. Modi departs for New Zealand on Friday, where he will face a different set of diplomatic dynamics before returning to India.

*Sources: Reuters, Dainik Bhaskar, The Indian Eye, Inshorts*
